reconcile.connective: Commentators read 'all Israel' as a future national ingathering distinct from the present unbelieving remnant Jesus threatens with exclusion in Matthew 8:12.

discrepancy.connective: Krister Stendahl reads Romans 11:26 as ethnic Israel's rescue apart from faith in Christ — a reading that widens, not closes, the gap with Matthew's threat.

skeptic.name: Krister Stendahl
skeptic.attribution: Krister Stendahl, Paul Among Jews and Gentiles (Fortress Press, 1976)

excerpts.excerpt_text: To understand this great statement, as some still do, merely of such a gradual inbringing of individual Jews, that there shall at length remain none in unbelief, is to do manifest violence both to it and to the whole context. It can only mean the ultimate ingathering of Israel as a nation, in contrast with the present "remnant."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles the tension by reframing 'all Israel' (Rom 11:26) as a future national ingathering distinct from the present unbelieving remnant Matt 8:12 excludes — different groups, different times, not a flat contradiction.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley pairs Matthew 8:12 directly against Romans 11:26 under 'Salvation — Extent: All Israel saved / Only a portion saved,' citing Alford, De Wette, Meyer, and Tholuck for the future-national-restoration reading, or alternatively 'the spiritual Israel' distinguished from Matthew's excluded 'children of the kingdom.'
